response:
**Recommendation:** Ship **Route B — UIKit/AVAudioEngine local-file player** first (AVAudioPlayerNode → AVAudioEnvironmentNode with `.HRTF` rendering algorithm → mainMixerNode → outputNode), operating only on locally-imported audio files (not SoundCloud streams).

**Why:**
- iOS 12.5 Safari has **no AudioWorklet** (added in 14.5). Real-time HRTF/binaural DSP in Route A would have to run on the deprecated **ScriptProcessorNode**, which executes on the main thread and reliably glitches/underruns on an A8 chip — this is the single biggest technical blocker for Route A, not a tuning problem.
- AVAudioEngine is native, hardware-accelerated, has shipped since iOS 8, and includes a purpose-built 3D/environmental audio node (`AVAudioEnvironmentNode`) with HRTF spatialization out of the box — far less engineering than hand-rolling PannerNode-based spatialization in JS.
- Route B has **zero SoundCloud ToS exposure** — it never touches third-party User Content, so there's no derivative-permission gating logic needed for the first release.
- Route C is legally and technically heavier: it requires (a) a permission-check/allowlist system per track before any processing, and (b) an AAC-HLS segment fetch → decrypt → decode-to-PCM pipeline via `AVAssetReader`/`AVURLAsset`, which is non-trivial even natively and would delay a usable release. It should be deferred to a v2 gated feature, not the first ship.
- Route A also inherits Safari-specific friction on old iOS (autoplay/gesture restrictions, background-audio limitations, memory-pressure eviction) that add risk without solving the DSP bottleneck.

**Next step:** Build a minimal native prototype: single-view iOS app, `AVAudioEngine` with `AVAudioPlayerNode -> AVAudioEnvironmentNode -> mainMixerNode`, set `environmentNode.renderingAlgorithm = .HRTF`, load one local test file (m4a/mp3), and manually verify binaural left/right/front/back positioning on wired headphones on an actual iPhone 6 running iOS 12.5.x. Measure CPU load and audio-thread stability under sustained playback (watch for `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChangeNotification` and buffer underrun logs) before adding any streaming/SoundCloud logic.

**Biggest trap:** Assuming Route A can be made "good enough" by optimizing JS — the lack of AudioWorklet on iOS 12.5 is a hard platform ceiling, not a tunable parameter, so no amount of buffer-size tweaking fixes ScriptProcessorNode glitching on this hardware/OS combo. A secondary trap: assuming Route C's legal gate ("uploader permits derivatives") is a one-time check — it must be re-validated per track/session since permissions can change, and the HLS-to-PCM decode step still needs to be built natively (Safari MSE/Web Audio cannot do this on iOS 12.5), so Route C effectively *also* requires most of Route B's native audio stack as a prerequisite.
